sections.html:
The Register of Deeds keeps Wilson County's real property and vital records. The county page lists deeds, deeds of trust, mortgage cancellations, powers of attorney, maps and many other documents among the papers it records.

The same office issues marriage licenses and holds the county's birth, death and marriage files, plus military discharges and notary oaths. For a house sale, only the real property side matters: the deed that moves title and the deed of trust that secures a buyer's loan both end up here. The register is an elected county officer, chosen every two years by the county's voters.

The office phone is 252-399-2935, and it is the number to use for most questions about a recording that is already in progress or a document you cannot find in the index. Marriage license visits and vital record amendments are scheduled by phone through that number.

The online search holds Wilson County's real estate indexes back to 1974, and older documents are still being scanned so their images can be viewed online. For an older chain of title, expect to ask the office for images that are not yet online.

Useful lookups before a sale include:

  • The current deed, to confirm how the owners' names appear.
  • Any deed of trust, to see whether a lender still has a lien.
  • Recorded cancellations, which show that an old loan was released.
  • Maps and plats that describe the lot lines.

Title searches for a closing are normally ordered by the closing attorney, but a quick index search lets an owner spot a stale lien early.

sections.h2: The delinquent tax statement on deeds
sections.html:
A deed has to carry a statement about delinquent property tax before the register accepts it. The county's deed requirements page explains that the rule dates from October 1, 2014 and rests on G.S. 161-31, which names Wilson County and which the commissioners implemented by resolution on December 6, 2004.

There are two routes. In the first, the paper is taken to the tax department's Collections Division, where a clerk confirms that no delinquent tax is owed. The attorney should have the parcel number printed on the deed or on hand. In the second, the attorney fills in the statement personally, and the deed can go straight to the register.

The county asks for separate checks, one for taxes owed and one for the Register of Deeds' recording fees. The tax department takes questions at 252-399-2900, option 2.

Every register in the state charges the same amounts, Wilson County included. An ordinary document costs $26.00 with 15 pages included. A loan security document starts at $64.00 and includes 35 pages. Extra pages on either are $4.00 apiece.

These fees are complete and exclusive, and they are collected before the document is filed. Nonstandard documents add $25.00, and each extra instrument in one document adds $10.00.

sections.h2: Who pays the deed stamp tax
sections.html:
The seller does. The state levy runs $1.00 for each $500 or fraction of value passing, and it is due to the register before filing.

One half is retained by the county and the other half is sent to the state monthly. Your closing attorney calculates it and deducts it at settlement, so ask for the exact number.

Protection against outside claims starts at registration in the land's home county. Contracts to convey, options, leases over three years and conveyances are not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value except from the time of registration, and priority follows the order of registration.

A seller who signs on Friday and a buyer who records the following week are both better off if the closing office records the same day. A seller who also owes tax should note that a deed without the tax statement cannot be filed in Wilson County.

sections.h2: Vital records at the same office
sections.html:
Certified copies of birth, death and marriage records can be ordered online, with pickup orders confirmed by a phone call, or requested by mail.

Adopted people born in Wilson County can now request new birth certificates directly from the register, in person only, under Senate Bill 248. Marriage license applicants print and fill out the application first, then call to book a visit, and only the couple attends. None of this affects a sale, but it explains why the front counter can be busy.

sections.h2: Ordering a certified copy of a deed
sections.html:
Search the online index first, since it lists real estate documents back to 1974, then request an image or a certified copy from the office. A certified copy runs $5.00 for its first page and $2.00 for each page that follows.

Deeds from before the online coverage may be missing from the images. A call to 252-399-2935 gets a clerk looking for the book and page. Heirs often need the deed that put title in the decedent's name, so order early to avoid delay during the contract period. A closing attorney or title company can also request the copy for you, which saves a trip to the counter in Wilson.

sections.h2: Common reasons a deed gets held up
sections.html:
Most delays come from the tax statement, not the recording itself. A deed brought to the register without either of the two tax options will not be accepted for recording, so the attorney has to go back to the tax department first.

Other frequent snags:

  • One check covering both taxes and recording fees, when the county asks for separate ones.
  • A missing parcel number, which slows the clerk's delinquent tax check.
  • A deed of trust left open after payoff, which keeps showing as a lien in the index.

If you hold a house inherited from a relative, the names on the last recorded deed may differ from the heirs. Sort that out with an attorney before a buyer's lender asks.

Gather the paperwork in the order the office will ask for it, starting with the tax statement since it is the item most likely to hold things up.

  • Find the parcel number in the county tax records.
  • Confirm the delinquent tax statement route with the closing attorney.
  • Bring two checks, one to the tax department and one to the register.
  • Ask whether any old deed of trust still needs a recorded cancellation.

A cash sale skips the lender's deed of trust, so the packet is shorter, but the tax statement and the recording fees still apply. Deeds move through this office steadily, with 411 building permits issued in 2025 across a county of 38,463 housing units.

faqs.q: Where is a Wilson County deed filed?
faqs.a: With the county Register of Deeds, reachable at 252-399-2935. For a sale, the closing attorney usually files it.

faqs.q: Does Wilson County require a tax statement on the deed?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts a deed only if it carries one of its two delinquent tax options, either verified by a tax department clerk or completed by the attorney.

faqs.q: What fee applies to a general deed in Wilson County?
faqs.a: An ordinary document costs $26.00 with 15 pages included, and each page past that adds $4.00. Loan security papers start at $64.00.

faqs.q: Who owes the excise tax on a Wilson County sale?
faqs.a: The seller, who pays the register before the deed is filed.

faqs.q: Can I search Wilson County deeds online?
faqs.a: Yes, for real estate indexes back to 1974. Older documents may not have images online yet, so ask the office about them.
